findings.title: The Disposal Plan Narrows into a Cavity
findings.claim: Within the declared pericope, the brothers' proposal to remove Yusuf narrows from lethal or spatial alternatives into hidden disposal whose later recovery is outsourced to strangers.
findings.mechanism: The focus imperatives kill and cast carry decisive removal and forceful throwing, while 12:10 independently negates killing and supplies casting, a hidden low place, a cut unlined well, and pickup by travelers; 12:15 then confirms the well as the executed destination. The contact changes the alternative from generic expulsion into an engineered cavity that keeps the body outside ordinary sight and responsibility.
findings.reader_payoff: The reader can see both the ordinary severity of the focus command and the concrete plot movement by which death is replaced with concealment, spatial subtraction, and a mediated handoff.
findings.containment: This is a grounded pericope relation. The focus still says kill or cast him to the ground; the hidden well and outsourced recovery belong to the later enacted narrowing, not to a replacement translation of the imperatives or a claim that concealment guarantees rescue.

epistemic.reason: The trusted channel supplies exact focus and context surfaces, the branch nominations, and the later execution that realizes the spatial alternative.

findings.title: Removal as Preemptive Rank Suppression
findings.claim: Within the declared pericope, the brothers' removal proposal can be read as anticipatory suppression of Yusuf's future recognition, not only as a reaction to present affection.
findings.mechanism: The focus face carries a contextual field of paternal regard and social standing. The dream's submission, the warning that the brothers may devise a stratagem, and Yusuf's promised selection independently supply a possible trajectory from affection to recognized rank; together they make the face an axis of anticipated status.
findings.reader_payoff: The reader can understand why removing Yusuf before the dream's elevation is recognized would look like preventive action against a future hierarchy, while still retaining the simpler jealousy reading.
findings.containment: This is a qualified HFT-supplied pericope inference. The text does not state that the brothers know the dream or act from it; the reading therefore remains a live anticipation layered over present favoritism.

epistemic.reason: The exact anchor surfaces and trace coordinates are supplied, but the context branch identities are legacy-unbound and the causal knowledge attributed to the brothers is inferential.

branch_activations.activation: Promised selection contacts the father's face as a possible social elevation visible through paternal regard.
branch_activations.resulting_reading: Removal can be heard as blocking a coming rise before it becomes public.
branch_activations.boundary: The selection branch remains attributed and does not prove that Yusuf's brothers know the promise.

branch_activations.resulting_reading: The proposed removal may preempt a hierarchy symbolized by Yusuf's later elevation.
branch_activations.boundary: The dream image is not converted into a direct prediction of political rank or a claim of disclosed knowledge.

findings.title: The Band Claims Corrective Authority
findings.claim: Within the declared pericope, the brothers' self-bounded band can frame its projected righteousness as authority to correct what it calls the father's misdirected distribution of love.
findings.mechanism: The focus face carries the field of paternal regard, while the focus peoplehood can name a male collective. Independently, 12:8 supplies Yusuf's belovedness, the brothers' mutually supporting band, and their diagnosis that the father is astray; the contact turns projected صالحين into a collective identity that presents redistribution as correction.
findings.reader_payoff: The reader can see how jealousy becomes more organized: the brothers do not merely want a larger share but can imagine their own cohesive group as the proper corrective authority.
findings.containment: This is a qualified HFT inference over 12:8-9. The ordinary readings of love, band, deviation, face, and peoplehood remain available, and the packet does not establish that the brothers' diagnosis is true or that the group possesses real moral authority.

epistemic.reason: The exact 12:8 and 12:9 surfaces are present, but the contextual branch descriptors and the move from grievance to authority are attributed inference.

findings.title: Disappearance Is Outsourced
findings.claim: Within the declared pericope, the alternative to killing is engineered as an indirect disappearance in which a hidden place and an unknowing traveling group carry the consequences away from the brothers.
findings.mechanism: The focus earth, killing, and casting surfaces meet 12:10's negation, cast-down body, low concealment, cut well, pickup, and traveling collective, then 12:15 confirms the placement. The contact changes banishment into a mediated transfer: the brothers make the first move, while strangers complete Yusuf's removal from their field.
findings.reader_payoff: The reader can track how moral distance is built materially: direct killing is rejected, Yusuf is lowered into a container, and an outside group is allowed to become the next agent of his fate.
findings.containment: This is a qualified HFT reading. The focus earth remains an ordinary, indefinite destination and the context may also be read as reducing harm; outsourcing and moral distance are an inference from the complete proposal, not a hidden lexical meaning of the focus forms.

epistemic.reason: The exact Arabic anchors and pericope sequence are supplied, while several traced context branches remain unresolved and the moral-distance conclusion is inferential.

findings.title: Care Language Becomes Access
findings.claim: Within the declared pericope, the brothers' language of trust, sincerity, and guardianship can function as a public credential that opens access to the very person they plan to remove.
findings.mechanism: The focus promises that after Yusuf's removal they will be صالحين, while 12:11 and 12:12 independently stage requests for trust, claims of freedom from fraud, and a promise to guard Yusuf. Their contact changes later righteousness from an untested moral conversion into a possible managed social identity that makes the plan permissible to the father.
findings.reader_payoff: The reader can feel the ethical predicates as operational: care language is not only decoration but the means by which the brothers seek permission and credibility before the act.
findings.containment: This is a qualified HFT reading. The brothers may be making sincere promises, and the focus can still project genuine moral improvement; the counterfeit-care layer is supported by the later violation but does not exhaust the dialogue.

epistemic.reason: The exact promises and focus word are present, but the branch roles are legacy-unbound and the inference from later violation to prior instrumentality remains interpretive.

branch_activations.resulting_reading: The very language of care can authorize the brothers' access to Yusuf before it is violated.
branch_activations.boundary: The promise remains a real statement in the scene; its counterfeit reading is a qualified retrospective pressure.

findings.title: Absence Does Not Empty the Father's Face
findings.claim: Within the declared pericope, Yusuf's absence can become another mode of presence because grief keeps the father's affect oriented toward the son the brothers tried to subtract.
findings.mechanism: The focus jussive يَخْلُ ordinarily projects a vacancy and the face وَجْهُ can represent the father's relational presence. The father's fear of separation, the brothers' staged crying, and his patient response independently show that removal does not empty the affective field; grief and restraint continue to organize it.
findings.reader_payoff: The reader can see why the brothers' zero-sum calculation is unstable: physical absence may intensify the father's attention to Yusuf rather than make that attention available to them.
findings.containment: This is a weakened HFT reading. The text may simply describe physical separation and a father's grief; the claim concerns the relational effect of absence, not a universal law that loss always increases presence.

epistemic.reason: The exact grief, crying, patience, and focus surfaces are supplied, but the claim that absence intensifies relational presence remains an attributed interpretation.

branch_activations.activation: Displayed grief contacts vacancy and shows that the removal immediately generates a new affective presence around the absent son.
branch_activations.resulting_reading: The brothers must manage the father's response because absence does not simply clear his attention.
branch_activations.boundary: The crying may be deceptive or merely part of the report; the activation does not make every grief performance false.

branch_activations.carrier: The father's fear of sorrow and separation in 12:13 is attributed as anticipatory grief around Yusuf's absence.
branch_activations.independent_trigger: The focus face supplies the father's relational field.
branch_activations.activation: Anticipated sorrow contacts the face and reveals that the father's attention remains organized by the son before the removal occurs.
branch_activations.resulting_reading: The plan targets a bond that is already expected to persist through absence.
branch_activations.boundary: The context establishes fear of grief, not a complete psychology of the father or a guaranteed result of the plan.

findings.title: The Afterward Keeps the Deed Alive
findings.claim: Within the declared pericope, the promised after-state is not a clean boundary behind the act but an incubation period in which the deed remains reportable and returns from the person the brothers tried to remove.
findings.mechanism: The focus بعدِهِ ordinarily establishes temporal afterness and تكونوا projects a future state of becoming. In 12:15, the completed well-plan is joined to a future disclosure by Yusuf while the brothers remain unaware; the contact changes aftermath from erasure into delayed transmissible news.
findings.reader_payoff: The reader can hold the brothers' projected new identity against the promise that their deed will re-enter the story through Yusuf's own report.
findings.containment: This is a qualified HFT reading of the exact 12:9 and 12:15 sequence. The future report need not cancel every possibility of repentance; it establishes latency and accountability pressure, not a complete later theology of the brothers.

epistemic.reason: The temporal and future-report surfaces are exact, while several context branch identities are unresolved and the interpretation of aftermath as incubation is attributed.

findings.title: The Group Authors Its Own Innocence
findings.claim: Within the declared pericope, the brothers' immediate aftermath models coordinated self-authorship: they manufacture affect and evidence so the group can continue to appear upright while controlling the father's interpretation.
findings.mechanism: The focus صالحين names a good or repaired state and وَجْهُ can represent the father's whole relational presence. The return scene independently supplies staged crying, a shirt, blood, explicit falsehood, self-decoration, and description; these concrete devices turn projected rectitude into reputational forensics before the father.
findings.reader_payoff: The reader can see exactly how the promised righteous identity is made visible: emotion, wearable evidence, material proof, and a narrated account work together to preserve the group's face.
findings.containment: This is a strengthened HFT reading of the supplied aftermath. The scene may still be a one-time alibi rather than a complete theory of their identity; the forensic mechanism exposes a live contradiction without replacing the ordinary future-state grammar.

epistemic.reason: The exact 12:16 and 12:18 evidence is supplied, but most traced branches are legacy-unbound and the coordinated authorship claim remains an inference from their combination.

findings.title: A Collective Stand-In
findings.claim: Exploratorily, the brothers seek to install their band itself in Yusuf's relational place before the father, becoming a collective stand-in after removal.
findings.mechanism: The focus vacancy, face, and qawm occur together after the removal proposal, while 12:8 supplies the mutually supporting band that feels displaced by Yusuf's belovedness. A form-distant substitution branch contacts this exact order and turns the band's future peoplehood into an image of taking the absent one's place.
findings.reader_payoff: The reader can see the brothers' plan as more than passive absence: the group imagines its own cohesion occupying the relational space that Yusuf currently holds.
findings.containment: This is an exploratory analogy, not the lexical meaning of قَوْمًا. Its substitution image is anchored in the vacancy-face-peoplehood sequence and the band in 12:8; it should be heard as an as-though mechanism subordinate to ordinary peoplehood.

epistemic.reason: The exact focus and 12:8 surfaces are supplied, but the substitution branch is form-distant and the contextual trace is legacy-unbound.

findings.title: A Graded Route Away from Killing
findings.claim: Exploratorily, the focus alternatives grade ways of breaking Yusuf's effective force in the paternal field, while the literal killing imperative remains dominant.
findings.mechanism: The focus ٱقْتُلُوا۟ carries literal life-taking and يَخْلُ names the cleared field. The focus-root side branch of reducing a drink's intensity and the later negation of killing plus casting in 12:10 contact those surfaces, creating a mechanism-level echo of reducing force without translating kill nonlethally.
findings.reader_payoff: The reader can distinguish the plot's moral and physical gradation: death is the harshest proposal, while casting is a lesser route toward the same intended clearing.
findings.containment: This is an exploratory cross-domain analogy. The drink-intensity branch is restricted to mixing drink with water and cannot replace the lethal sense; the shared result is a bounded mechanism-level comparison.

epistemic.reason: The exact focus and 12:10 alternatives are supplied, but the tempering branch is cross-domain and its contact with the plot is an attributed analogy.

findings.title: The Face as an Unguarded Resource
findings.claim: Exploratorily, the brothers imagine Yusuf's removal as exposing an unguarded relational resource that their band can seize before the father.
findings.mechanism: The focus vacancy can ordinarily describe a field lacking what should be in it, while the focus face supplies the father's relational presence. The promise to guard Yusuf in 12:12 independently reverses into a scene where removing the guarded one opens the desired field, creating a predatory spatial analogy.
findings.reader_payoff: The reader can feel the brothers' desire as active appropriation: they do not simply await attention but imagine the father's availability becoming open to them.
findings.containment: This is an exploratory HFT analogy. The unguarded branch requires the absence of a protector and a resulting target; the verse does not say the father lacks protection, so the image remains a local pressure on the clearing construction.

epistemic.reason: The exact focus and guardianship surfaces are supplied, but the unguarded-resource contact is form-distant and attributed.

branch_activations.resulting_reading: The brothers' care language makes their later seizure of the father's field appear more predatory.
branch_activations.boundary: The reversal is contextual and does not prove that the promise was consciously designed to enable harm.

findings.containment: This is a medium-confidence exploratory analogy. The garment-that-lies image is not the syntax or lexical meaning of the focus; it is grounded only in the actual shirt, blood, and falsehood placed beside the projected righteous identity.

findings.title: Fatiha Adds an Upright-Path Overlay
findings.claim: As a local Fatiha overlay, the phrase ٱلْمُسْتَقِيمَ can make the focus qawm's projected righteousness sound like a collective standard of remaining upright and on a straight path.
findings.mechanism: The focus قَوْمًا ordinarily names a male collective. The external occurrence ٱلْمُسْتَقِيمَ in 1:6 carries the supplied uprightness, balance, and non-deviation branch; contact between the two adds an explicit straight-path criterion to the group's projected identity.
findings.reader_payoff: The reader can hear صالحين as more than a generic moral label in the overlay: the promised group is imaginable as one that must remain straight, balanced, and non-deviating.
findings.containment: This is an exploratory Phase 2 overlay only. It does not replace qawm's peoplehood or the focus's native moral claim, does not make qawm mean path, and does not import the whole theme of Fatiha or the whole surah into 12:9.

epistemic.reason: The focus qawm branch and the exact external straight-path occurrence are present, but the overlay is a writer-level cross-text contact without a supplied candidate or connection record.

branch_activations.independent_trigger: Fatiha's ٱلْمُسْتَقِيمَ names a straight, balanced, non-deviating path in 1:6.
branch_activations.activation: The external straight-path criterion contacts the focus group at the point where it projects a future righteous identity.
branch_activations.resulting_reading: The group can be heard as collectively answerable to remaining upright rather than merely claiming a moral name.
branch_activations.boundary: The overlay is contextual and local; it does not transfer path meaning into qawm or determine the native reading.
